conventions.convention: Local-stochastic noise bounds the probability that every location in each specified subset faults by η raised to that subset's cardinality; η^0=1. Independence is not assumed.

A schedule is finite and chronological, includes only explicitly scheduled idles, and assigns each replacement channel its original location's support. Pattern-dependent replacements do not introduce an additional joint operation across slots.

Full-space CPTP deviation and encoded-instrument error sectors are different relations. Encoded branches retain their subnormalized probabilities and need not extend to full-space CPTP error maps. Other live blocks belong to the joint data system; only the external reference is unchanged.

The proper-code parameter d is correction capacity, not stabilizer distance. The concrete construction declares d=2 and effective spread budget one despite having stabilizer distance nine and ideal recovery through weight four.

Ordinary child rectangles partition their elementary locations. Extended rectangles can overlap and instead require the separate reverse scan with expanded-support truncation, including lower-scale input collars.

Noisy guarantees start on encoded inputs or protected prescribed preparations. Unknown-input encoding is guaranteed only without faults; final noisy classical readout emits an encoded classical block.
Universality means full operator-norm density, including scalar phases. The added scalar generator is P=exp(2πi√2)I, and no controlled scalar operation is identified with an identity channel.

The planar memory theorem uses d≥2, n=2d² physical edges, left/right rough boundaries, independent Z errors, perfect syndrome extraction and minimum-cardinality recovery. It does not assert a faulty-gate threshold.

load_bearing.statement: For every integer q≥1 with 2qℓ≤d, the computation-stage contract takes incoming joint error budget qℓ and at most q bad children to output budget 2qℓ; correction corrects admitted budget at most d and returns residual budget qℓ with the same decoded logical channel. The physical alphabet is closed under recursive replacement.

Zero-fault correction maps every input into the code and corrects the weight-at-most-four Pauli span. On weight-at-most-two inputs, at most one faulty location leaves the original logical state with a weight-at-most-one residual error. With at most one fault, arbitrary inputs are attracted into the weight-one code-error range without a logical-preservation assertion.

If each computation stage and its correction stage have at most q bad child rectangles and 2qℓ≤d, then after each correction stage the joint output instrument has error budget at most d after its ideal encoded target; declared decoded recovery returns that ideal target exactly, retaining every finite external reference.

For the full-depth disjoint-child hierarchy with badness requiring q+1 bad children, an η-local-stochastic law gives root bad probability at most A^(-1/q)(A^(1/q)η)^((q+1)^r), where A=binomial(a,q+1) and Aη^q<1. No independence assumption is used.

Under the stated checked local gadget, decoder, explicit-port and expanded-support truncation hypotheses, good complete or truncated exRecs are correct. Selected bad level-r roots have disjoint full binary witness trees, with at most A^(2^r−1) labelled trees per root and joint probability at most (A^(2^r−1)η^(2^r))^k for k specified selected bad roots.

The displayed W=V tensor-power seven composed with V encodes an explicit [[49,1,9]] stabilizer code, has fixed exact decoded recovery through weight four, and implements exact transversal H, S and coordinate-paired CNOT with the stated phases and support bounds.

Encoded error instruments need not have full-space CPTP extensions in the same error span. Nevertheless, a fixed recovery correcting the normalized mixture of all weight-at-most-s Paulis corrects every trace-preserving encoded instrument in their span, including joint blocks and finite external references.

On logical failure of minimum-cardinality perfect-syndrome Z recovery, E symmetric-difference R contains a self-avoiding left-to-right path P with d≤|P|≤n and at least ceiling(|P|/2) actual error edges.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite fault-pattern laws, nonnegative normalized weights and finite outcome averaging.
Cardinalities of finite location and witness sets, including the empty set.
Mutual independence of elementary indicators and events determined by disjoint location sets.
Full-unitary density and the norm used in the universality contract.
Homogeneity and the triangle inequality in the scalar-phase density argument.
Finite unions of witness events, bad rectangles and planar crossing-path events.

concerns.concern: Proof 2.1 concludes: 'Induction over the finite sequence of computation and correction stages at each concatenation level gives joint encoded error budget at most qℓ≤d'. Steps 1.1–1.3 establish the alternating-stage invariant only when the asserted stage contracts already apply. They do not establish the induction from level r to r+1: no hierarchical error sector or recursive decoder is defined here, and no argument shows that an arbitrary bad child's potentially unencoded output becomes an admissible coarse fault while good children retain their attached syndromes. The cited proper-code definition specifies encoded-input budgets and zero-fault arbitrary-input correction, but supplies no proved recursive substitution or noisy arbitrary-input attraction result. This is substantial for both general threshold consumers. The concrete existence theorem separately supplies hierarchical sectors and attraction/substitution arguments in 2.3 and 5.2–7.1, but this general lemma neither cites nor generalizes those arguments. Source comparison: Aharonov–Ben-Or, https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/9611025, Appendix C, pp. 12–14, explicitly proves three simultaneous recursive assertions, including arbitrary-input correction. If the present contracts are intended to assume their identities at every level, that additional hypothesis needs to be explicit; otherwise the recursive correctness claim remains unsupported.

The Statement says 'let p_r be a uniform upper bound ... with p_0=η' and then asserts 'p_{r+1}≤A p_r^{q+1}'. This is false for an arbitrary sequence of uniform upper bounds. For example, take η=0, a=2, q=1 and a full binary hierarchy: every actual bad probability is zero, but p_0=0 and p_r=1 for r≥1 are valid uniform upper bounds and violate p_1≤0. Proof 1.2 bounds the actual parent probability by A p_r^{q+1}; it does not bound a previously arbitrary p_{r+1}. The intended recursively chosen envelope, or the supremum of actual bad probabilities, must be specified. The closed-form bound is sound for that intended choice.

seams_checked.note: Channel and composition suppliers use full operator spaces and CP/TP maps. Schedule composition and finite averaging preserve those domains; no physical implementation is inferred from the mathematical channel definition.

Chronological order, explicit observed records and subnormalized instrument branches are retained. The concrete gadgets specify and charge physical controls rather than inferring free controlled access.
Support and weight use the declared tensor factors and wire permutations. Detection alone is not cited as recovery; recovery claims use the additional Knill–Laflamme and stabilizer suppliers.

Exact recovery is used as an equality of logical channels with finite references. Uniform recovery on error spans is separately derived; encoded instruments are explicitly distinguished from full-space CPTP error maps.
Pauli signs and exact H, S and T phases match the suppliers. The twice-concatenated S identity accounts for the seven-qubit code's S-adjoint action.

CSS nesting, scalar-phase stabilizer quotients and 2t<distance are preserved. The planar argument uses the supplied relative patch, crossing direction and path-count bound; its minimum-weight half-error witness is proved locally.

The threshold arguments use D=one-half the trace norm, D≤1 and finite-POVM variation≤D with the correct factors. The sparse-path concern affects their premise of ideal decoded output on good patterns, rather than citation fidelity at this seam.
The supplier establishes projective Clifford+T density. The batch does not silently strengthen it to U(2) density: it adds an irrational scalar generator and proves the full-phase extension locally.
